formula_checks.name: basePay
formula_checks.reviewer_why: The household tax row uses gross×household rate even in mixed entered/calculated take-home mode, while actual implied deductions can differ by earner. Its bracket is wages-only despite the owner’s all-income band rule.
formula_checks.reviewer_should_be: Expose each entered/calculated component distinctly, reconcile gross−deductions−401(k)=take-home, and use one all-taxable-income band producer.
formula_checks.what_the_code_actually_does: Two points. (1) The band: basePay reads the band of the wages less the 401(k)s (marginalBracketFor on wages), while DEC-0178 says the band is worked out ONCE from everything taxed together. $60,000 of wages and $50,000 of rent, single: the card says 12%; the household’s band is 22%, and the card’s own tax is worked at the all-income rate (13.97%). APP WRONG. (2) The mixed-mode tax row: basePay still returns tax.monthly = gross × rate, but the screen draws NO household tax row in a mixed household (BasePayScreen shows the tax row only in mode "estimated"; DEC-0207 frame 2a-iii) — REVIEWER WRONG on that point.
formula_checks.fixed_2026_10_25: FIXED 2026-10-25 (FIX-INCOME-A, landed 2026-10-26): the band on everything taxed (DEC-0178); each "/month" a paid month's; an hourly wage with no hours shows no total.

But no screen asks the hours (BasePayScreen has no hours field; hoursPerWeek is written nowhere), so every hourly wage is read as a 40-hour week and nothing says so: $25 an hour → $4,333.33 a month.

The blank-to-$0 the reviewer describes happens there: BasePayScreen stores a cleared cell as "" and salaryMonths reads it as a typed $0 month. formula_checks.name: grossByMonth
